chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man pray any of the obligatory prayers while riding?' He said, 'No, except out of necessity.'
ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to pray obligatory prayers while riding in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the default state for obligatory prayers is standing, riding is permitted solely under conditions of genuine necessity (*darurah*), such as illness or travel difficulty. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *ease in hardship* (*al-yusr*), ensuring that religious obligations remain accessible without imposing undue burden on the believer.
